brevity.meaning: [EW] Land or surface emitter activity detected via communications intelligence. Opposite of ASLEEP.
brevity.source: ATP 1-02.1 Multi-Service Brevity Codes (BMS Docs\04 Other Documentation\Real Manuals)

brevity.meaning: [A/S] [S/A] Release or launch of specified weapon at designated target (e.g., 1 AWAY, 2 PIGS AWAY, BIRDS AWAY, etc.). At minimum number or weapon type required. NOTE Include launch location in BULLSEYE format and weapons track direction when appropriate.
brevity.source: ATP 1-02.1 Multi-Service Brevity Codes (BMS Docs\04 Other Documentation\Real Manuals)

brevity.meaning: 1. [A/A] [AIR-MAR] A picture label describing two GROUPs separated laterally. GROUP names will be referenced by cardinal directions (e.g., NORTH GROUP, SOUTH GROUP, or EAST GROUP, WEST GROUP). 2. [S/A] Direction to the threat.
brevity.source: ATP 1-02.1 Multi-Service Brevity Codes (BMS Docs\04 Other Documentation\Real Manuals)

brevity.meaning: [A/S] Informative call that the displayed map is unusable due to the following: (U) Terrain - informative call that shadows obstruct the target area and a map must be taken from a different axis or graze angle. (U) Image - informative call that the displayed image quality prevents target identification (ID).
brevity.source: ATP 1-02.1 Multi-Service Brevity Codes (BMS Docs\04 Other Documentation\Real Manuals)

brevity.meaning: [A/A] [AIR-MAR] Positively identified as an enemy IAW theater ID criteria. The term does not imply direction or authority to engage. [SO] A SUSPECT whose orbital parameters are such that it may become a collection and/or counterspace concern to a spacecraft in the relative near-term, therefore limiting decision space.
brevity.source: ATP 1-02.1 Multi-Service Brevity Codes (BMS Docs\04 Other Documentation\Real Manuals)
brevity.bmsUsage: GCI example: used for a suspected hostile aircraft.

brevity.source: ATP 1-02.1 Multi-Service Brevity Codes (BMS Docs\04 Other Documentation\Real Manuals)
brevity.bmsUsage: "Launch and decide": FOX3 before DR, elements notch opposite directions for a pre-briefed time (commonly 15 s); if spiked abort, if naked turn in and press.

brevity.meaning: Reference number used to indicate such information as headings, altitude, fuels, etc.

brevity.source: ATP 1-02.1 Multi-Service Brevity Codes (BMS Docs\04 Other Documentation\Real Manuals)

brevity.meaning: [A/A] [A/S] Potential JAMMER along the stated azimuth from a ground unit or aircraft stated from the unit or aircraft's location. Usually followed by a request to search using an alternate radar source.
brevity.source: ATP 1-02.1 Multi-Service Brevity Codes (BMS Docs\04 Other Documentation\Real Manuals)

brevity.meaning: AWACS aspect: 120-80 deg.

brevity.meaning: Pre-briefed fuel state needed for recovery.
brevity.source: ATP 1-02.1 Multi-Service Brevity Codes (BMS Docs\04 Other Documentation\Real Manuals)
brevity.bmsUsage: Fuel state set on the DED BINGO page; Betty calls "BINGO BINGO" when reached (example 3000 lbs).

brevity.meaning: [S/A] FRIENDLY SAM(s). Modifiers include: AWAY, NEGATE, AFFIRM.
brevity.source: ATP 1-02.1 Multi-Service Brevity Codes (BMS Docs\04 Other Documentation\Real Manuals)

brevity.meaning: [SO] Signal is on the air with zero content.
brevity.source: ATP 1-02.1 Multi-Service Brevity Codes (BMS Docs\04 Other Documentation\Real Manuals)

brevity.meaning: No visual contact with FRIENDLY aircraft, ship or ground position. Opposite of VISUAL.
brevity.source: ATP 1-02.1 Multi-Service Brevity Codes (BMS Docs\04 Other Documentation\Real Manuals)
brevity.bmsUsage: Wingman lost visual on lead - call "Blind".

brevity.meaning: [MAR-MAR] An inherently defensive tactic used to force a vessel to alter course away from the defended asset or stop its closure. It is accomplished by maneuvering a unit directly in front of the closing vessel and maintaining position. The possibility of collision exists, depending on the intent of the closing vessel.
brevity.source: ATP 1-02.1 Multi-Service Brevity Codes (BMS Docs\04 Other Documentation\Real Manuals)

brevity.meaning: [EW] electronic countermeasure receiver.
brevity.source: ATP 1-02.1 Multi-Service Brevity Codes (BMS Docs\04 Other Documentation\Real Manuals)

brevity.source: ATP 1-02.1 Multi-Service Brevity Codes (BMS Docs\04 Other Documentation\Real Manuals)

brevity.meaning: [A/A] Informative call that the intercepting aircraft is dropping targeting responsibility and commencing a BLOW THROUGH.
brevity.source: ATP 1-02.1 Multi-Service Brevity Codes (BMS Docs\04 Other Documentation\Real Manuals)

brevity.meaning: Radar being jammed.
brevity.source: ATP 1-02.1 Multi-Service Brevity Codes (BMS Docs\04 Other Documentation\Real Manuals)

brevity.source: ATP 1-02.1 Multi-Service Brevity Codes (BMS Docs\04 Other Documentation\Real Manuals)

brevity.meaning: A deck landing where the hook misses all 4 wires.
brevity.source: BMS Naval Ops

brevity.meaning: [S/A] Track identified as a separated booster phase component of a ballistic missile.
brevity.source: ATP 1-02.1 Multi-Service Brevity Codes (BMS Docs\04 Other Documentation\Real Manuals)

brevity.meaning: Bomb On Target: aircraft must be tally on the target (eyeball or sensor); good weather, guided/unguided or strafe.
brevity.source: BMS Training Manual 4.38.1, Mission 27 (JTAC / CAS)

brevity.meaning: [A/A] [AIR-MAR] Picture label with GROUPs in a square or offset square.
brevity.source: ATP 1-02.1 Multi-Service Brevity Codes (BMS Docs\04 Other Documentation\Real Manuals)

brevity.meaning: [A/A] [S/A] 1. The following information is in a tactical control format providing target bearing, range, altitude, and aspect (BRAA) relative to the specified FRIENDLY aircraft. 2. Switch to BRAA format to a specific GROUP or CONTACT.
brevity.source: ATP 1-02.1 Multi-Service Brevity Codes (BMS Docs\04 Other Documentation\Real Manuals)

brevity.source: ATP 1-02.1 Multi-Service Brevity Codes (BMS Docs\04 Other Documentation\Real Manuals)

brevity.meaning: [A/A] Perform an immediate maximum performance turn in the indicated direction (default is a 180-degree turn).
brevity.source: ATP 1-02.1 Multi-Service Brevity Codes (BMS Docs\04 Other Documentation\Real Manuals)

brevity.meaning: Tanker or receiver call indicating immediate vertical and nose-to-tail separation between tanker and receiver is required.
brevity.source: ATP 1-02.1 Multi-Service Brevity Codes (BMS Docs\04 Other Documentation\Real Manuals)

brevity.source: ATP 1-02.1 Multi-Service Brevity Codes (BMS Docs\04 Other Documentation\Real Manuals)

brevity.source: ATP 1-02.1 Multi-Service Brevity Codes (BMS Docs\04 Other Documentation\Real Manuals)

brevity.source: ATP 1-02.1 Multi-Service Brevity Codes (BMS Docs\04 Other Documentation\Real Manuals)

brevity.word: BUDDY SPIKE [position or heading or altitude]

brevity.source: ATP 1-02.1 Multi-Service Brevity Codes (BMS Docs\04 Other Documentation\Real Manuals)
brevity.bmsUsage: AI command/radio call telling a friendly who has locked you that the contact he bugged is a friendly.

brevity.source: ATP 1-02.1 Multi-Service Brevity Codes (BMS Docs\04 Other Documentation\Real Manuals)

brevity.meaning: [S/S] FRIENDLY surface or submarine launched anti-ship missile.
brevity.source: ATP 1-02.1 Multi-Service Brevity Codes (BMS Docs\04 Other Documentation\Real Manuals)

brevity.meaning: [AIR-MAR] Maritime aircraft patrol zone.

brevity.source: ATP 1-02.1 Multi-Service Brevity Codes (BMS Docs\04 Other Documentation\Real Manuals)

brevity.source: ATP 1-02.1 Multi-Service Brevity Codes (BMS Docs\04 Other Documentation\Real Manuals)

brevity.source: ATP 1-02.1 Multi-Service Brevity Codes (BMS Docs\04 Other Documentation\Real Manuals)

brevity.source: ATP 1-02.1 Multi-Service Brevity Codes (BMS Docs\04 Other Documentation\Real Manuals)

brevity.source: ATP 1-02.1 Multi-Service Brevity Codes (BMS Docs\04 Other Documentation\Real Manuals)

brevity.source: ATP 1-02.1 Multi-Service Brevity Codes (BMS Docs\04 Other Documentation\Real Manuals)

brevity.source: ATP 1-02.1 Multi-Service Brevity Codes (BMS Docs\04 Other Documentation\Real Manuals)
brevity.bmsUsage: Carrier: signal/clearance for aircraft to land - "cleared to enter the landing pattern" / begin the approach procedure.

brevity.meaning: Begin using briefed communication procedures to counter communications jamming. If no modifier specified, "radio" is understood.
brevity.source: ATP 1-02.1 Multi-Service Brevity Codes (BMS Docs\04 Other Documentation\Real Manuals)

brevity.meaning: [A/A] Active missile data link terminated between high and medium pulse repetition frequency (MPRF) active.
brevity.source: ATP 1-02.1 Multi-Service Brevity Codes (BMS Docs\04 Other Documentation\Real Manuals)

brevity.meaning: [A/A] Turn (number) degrees left or right and maintain new heading.
brevity.source: ATP 1-02.1 Multi-Service Brevity Codes (BMS Docs\04 Other Documentation\Real Manuals)

brevity.meaning: Target appears to be no longer tracked by sensor.
brevity.source: ATP 1-02.1 Multi-Service Brevity Codes (BMS Docs\04 Other Documentation\Real Manuals)

brevity.meaning: Reference specified medium for message traffic (internet relay chat [IRC], J28.2, etc.).
brevity.source: ATP 1-02.1 Multi-Service Brevity Codes (BMS Docs\04 Other Documentation\Real Manuals)

brevity.source: ATP 1-02.1 Multi-Service Brevity Codes (BMS Docs\04 Other Documentation\Real Manuals)

brevity.source: ATP 1-02.1 Multi-Service Brevity Codes (BMS Docs\04 Other Documentation\Real Manuals)

brevity.meaning: 1. [A/A] No sensor information on a GROUP of interest. 2. No visible battle damage. 3. Aircraft not carrying external stores.

brevity.meaning: Requested action is authorized. NOTE Engaged support roles not established or transferred.
brevity.source: ATP 1-02.1 Multi-Service Brevity Codes (BMS Docs\04 Other Documentation\Real Manuals)

brevity.meaning: 1. [A/S] Term used by a joint terminal attack controller (JTAC)/forward air controller (airborne) (FAC(A)) during Type 3 control, granting a weapons release clearance to an aircraft or flight to attack a target or targets within the parameters prescribed by the JTAC/FAC(A). 2. [A/A] [A/S] Clearance to fire on designated GROUP or target.
brevity.source: ATP 1-02.1 Multi-Service Brevity Codes (BMS Docs\04 Other Documentation\Real Manuals)

brevity.meaning: [EW] Jamming signal.

brevity.meaning: [A/A] Decreasing separation.

casCheckIn.title: CAS Routing & Aircraft Check-in (CAS sheet page 1)

routing.description: Initial contact on the briefed JTAC/FAC(A) frequency: intentions, position, deconfliction by keyhole template (echo point + sector/distance + altitude block) and system readback.
exampleExchange: JTAC: "Cyborg 7, Eyeball 9, read you 5/5, say intention."
CAS: "Eyeball 9, Cyborg 7, CAS capable, ready for check-in."
JTAC: "Cyborg 7, Eyeball 9, say current position and altitude."
JTAC: "Cyborg 7, hold position, climb 20000, keyhole template in effect, advise when ready to copy coordinates."

JTAC: "Cyborg 7, Echo Point North 37 08 060, East 130 20 021, Proceed B 25 and hold between B25-35, left hand pattern, Angels 20-22, Report established, hold your check-in, Attack in progress. Bone 1 on station, 2 ship F-15E, C25, Block 22-24, System Readback."
CAS: "Eyeball 9, Cyborg 7, System Readback. North 37 08 060, East 130 20 021, Proceed B 25 angels 20-22, Will report when established."
CAS (at holding): "Eyeball 9, Cyborg 7, Established Bravo 25, left hand pattern 10 mile leg B 25-35, Blk 20-22, ready for check-in."
routing.source: BMS Training Manual 4.38.1, Mission 27 (JTAC / CAS) 27.2 (1); BMS Kneeboard Templates - Close Air Support 3/4

lines.label: SITREPs / Codes

lines.example: Cyborg 7 has Sit-rep alpha passed by Magic 7

lines.label: Map

casCheckIn.exampleCall: Eyeball 9, Cyborg 7, Mission number 2024, two by F-16C, Currently Bravo 25, block 20-22, 510 rounds of 20 mike mike, four by GBU-54 each aircraft, Nose/Tail fusing, Laser code 1688 each aircraft, Playtime four zero minutes, FAC(A) capable, Sniper, IDM 11 and 12 sweet, Abort Code: Oscar November.

notes: Only the flight lead checks in for the flight.
The line numbering above follows the order of the BMS CAS sheet / Training Manual list; the sheet itself numbers items 3-18 together with the routing fields.

BMS AI JTAC: check-in starts directly without authentication and includes package number, type/number of aircraft, position/altitude relative to the JTAC, loadout (no specific ordnance type) and playtime. Echo point coordinates are passed after the check-in.
casCheckIn.source: BMS Training Manual 4.38.1, Mission 27 (JTAC / CAS) 27.2 (2), 27.3; BMS Kneeboard Templates - Close Air Support 3/4

nineLine.title: CAS 9-Line Brief

gamePlan.description: Given before the 9-line (no readback needed): type of control, attack method, ordnance type/number, ripple/interval, fuse settings, burst altitude.

fields.label: Type control
fields.description: Type 1: JTAC/FAC(A) visual on target AND attacking aircraft. Type 2: visual on target OR aircraft. Type 3: visual on neither.

fields.label: Attack method
fields.description: BOC (Bomb On Coordinate - no tally required, bad weather, GPS/LGB) or BOT (Bomb On Target - tally required, good weather, guided/unguided/strafe).

fields.label: Type + number ordnance
fields.description: Specific type and amount of ordnance requested.

fields.label: Ripple + interval
fields.description: When releasing multiple weapons in one attack.

fields.label: Fuse settings
fields.description: BMS: Nose, Tail or N/T (all instantaneous); delayed/airburst not available.

gamePlan.example: Cyborg 71, Eyeball 9. Type 2, Bomb on coordinate. One by GBU-54, Laser mode, N/T fusing, Advise when ready for 9-line.

lines.label: IP/BP
lines.description: Initial point (or battle position) for the attack - in the example the holding point. BMS JTAC: distance in NM.

lines.label: Heading + offset
lines.description: Magnetic heading from the IP to the target; offset = side of the IP-to-target line where the aircraft may maneuver to arrive at the final attack heading. With the BMS JTAC use line 2 as final attack heading (remarks/restrictions not implemented).

lines.label: Distance
lines.description: Distance from the IP to the target (NM).

lines.label: Target elevation
lines.description: Target elevation in feet (MSL). Read back with line 6.

lines.label: Target description
lines.description: Target type and number of units.

lines.label: Target location
lines.description: LAT/LONG coordinates or bullseye; "Visual / Offset" for talk-ons or when no LAT/LONG is available. Read back with line 4 (system readback).

lines.label: Type mark / terminal guidance
lines.description: Marking provided by the JTAC/FAC(A): None, Willie Pete (phosphorus munition), Smoke, Sparkle (infrared pointer), Laser (with laser code). The BMS JTAC only mentions smoke but is laser capable too.

lines.label: Friendlies
lines.description: Position of the nearest friendly forces relative to the target (BMS JTAC gives meters). Some air forces require its readback.

lines.label: Egress
lines.description: Post-attack direction and position.

nineLine.exampleCall: Cyborg 71, Eyeball 9. Bravo 25. Heading 270. Right. 25 miles. 2854 feet. Single truck in the open. North 37 07 059. East 130 20 011. Laser, Sparkle, Smoke, 3 miles east, Left B25. Advise when ready for remarks and restrictions.
remarks: Everything important to secure aircrew and ground forces must be (re)mentioned.
restrictions: Final attack heading - given clockwise as a cone (e.g. "220 clockwise 250").
Altitude - minimum altitude to avoid MANPADS/gunfire/terrain (e.g. "Stay above 15000").
TOT / TTT - Time Over Target (impact time) or Time To Target (delta from a time hack: "TIME TO TARGET 5 minutes. READY, READY, HACK").
nineLine.remarksRestrictionsExample: Cyborg 71, Eyeball 9, Remarks. Manpad near TGT. Wind 15kts from the west, few clouds. Eyeball 9 will be lasing with laser code 1688 at IP inbound call, confirm SPOT. Restrictions. Final attack heading 220 clockwise 250. Stay above 15000. TOT 15:25. System readback line 4 + 6, All remarks/restrictions. How copy?
nineLine.readbackExample: Eyeball 9, Cyborg 71. System readback. 2854 feet. North 37 07 059. East 130 20 011. Remarks. MANPAD near target... Restrictions. Final attack heading 220 clockwise 250. Staying above 15000. TOT 15:25z.
notes: Do not read back the 9-line until remarks/restrictions are received; then read back lines 4 and 6 (and 8 in some air forces).
For BOC a system readback is indispensable; for BOT it is not required (tally is the backup verification).

VIP use: when the IP is a marked location, set a markpoint/steerpoint as VIP with target bearing/range/elevation, slew the VIP onto the mark and toggle the SPI to the target (CZ reverses changes; STPT and VIP elevation must match).
BMS AI JTAC 9-line units: lines 1 and 3 in NM, line 4 in feet, line 8 in meters.
nineLine.source: BMS Training Manual 4.38.1, Mission 27 (JTAC / CAS) 27.2 (4)-(7), 27.3; BMS Kneeboard Templates - Close Air Support 5/6

sitrep.title: Situation Report (SITREP)

lines.label: Threat
lines.description: Surface-to-air threat activity.

lines.label: Enemy situation
lines.description: Enemy activity / target.

lines.label: Friendly
lines.description: Friendly situation and positions.

lines.label: Artillery
lines.description: Artillery activity.

lines.label: Clearance authority
lines.description: Who has control / clearance authority.

lines.label: Hazards
lines.description: Hazards in the area (plus controller's intent and ordnance where relevant).

lines.label: Remarks / restrictions
lines.description: Remarks and restrictions.

sitrep.exampleCall: Eyeball 9 to all flights on station, new Sitrep. Sitrep Bravo is now in effect: Current surface-to-air threat is an SA-8 at Delta 15, just west of Hwangji; target is a light armored resupply battalion to flank us to the left, break. Friendlies are one infantry battalion 3 miles east of the target, break. Eyeball 9 has control and is part of the friendly battalion. Plan on using your GBU-54 bombs to disrupt the trucks. Winds on the deck are 15 knots out of the east. Eyeball 9 is laser and sparkle capable, advise when ready for game plan.
notes: Key element order: Threat -> Enemy situation -> Friendlies -> Clearance authority -> Controller's intent -> Hazards -> Remarks/Restrictions.
A sitrep code (e.g. "Sitrep Bravo") can be generated and passed to CAS flights and C2/AWACS to reduce workload.
No readback required; questions in plain language. The BMS AI JTAC does not implement the sitrep.
sitrep.source: BMS Training Manual 4.38.1, Mission 27 (JTAC / CAS) 27.2 (3); BMS Kneeboard Templates - Close Air Support 3/4

authentication.description: On unsecure communications (BMS UHF/VHF is unsecure) CAS parties authenticate with pre-briefed codes, e.g. a ramrod codeword or authentication tables (AKAC 1553, etc.). The Training Manual uses the 2-letter ramrod: a codeword whose letters each appear only once (the BMS list uses 10-letter words; the manual says most ramrod words have 11 letters). Authentication proves both sides are authorized and friendly.
authentication.howTo: The challenger names the codeword in effect and two letters; the responder answers with the letter found BETWEEN those two letters in the codeword. Example with code word "Bravo 1" = SOUNDTRACK: JTAC "Cyborg 7, Eyeball 9, Code word Bravo 1 in effect, Authenticate Tango Alpha." -> in S-O-U-N-D-T-R-A-C-K the letter between T and A is R -> CAS "Eyeball 9, Cyborg 7, Authenticate Romeo." -> JTAC "Cyborg 7, Eyeball 9, send your check-in." The abort code is generated the same way: abort code "Oscar November" -> letter between O and N is U, so the abort call is "ABORT UNIFORM, ABORT UNIFORM, ABORT UNIFORM" (answer: "Cyborg 7 aborts the pass").
authentication.matrix: CAS_Authentication_Matrix kneeboard: blank 26 x 26 grid (First Letter A-Z across, Second Letter A-Z down) for an authentication table.
notes: The BMS AI JTAC starts the check-in without authentication.
authentication.source: BMS Training Manual 4.38.1, Mission 27 (JTAC / CAS) 27.2 (2), 27.3; BMS Kneeboard Templates - Close Air Support 2, 3, 7

casProcedure.title: 12 Steps of CAS

steps.name: Routing / Safety of Flight
steps.description: Contact JTAC/FAC(A), clarify intentions, deconflict from other aircraft, surface threats and hazards; keyhole holding assignment and system readback. (BMS JTAC: not implemented - fly to your holding, e.g. B25-35 Block 20-22.)

steps.name: CAS Aircraft Check-in
steps.description: Authentication, then flight lead check-in; JTAC reads back only the abort code. (BMS JTAC: radio menu option 1 twice.)

steps.name: Situation Update
steps.description: SITREP - no readback. (BMS JTAC: not implemented.)

steps.name: Game Plan
steps.description: Type of control, attack method, ordnance and settings - no readback. (BMS JTAC gives type of control after the echo point.)

steps.name: CAS Brief / 9-line
steps.description: Attack plan in 9 lines. (BMS JTAC: option 2 "Ready for Echo Point/9-line", press again for the 9-line.)

steps.name: Remarks / Restrictions
steps.description: Threats, weather, hazards, marks, final attack heading, altitude, TOT/TTT. (BMS JTAC: not implemented - use line 2 as final attack heading.)

steps.name: Readbacks
steps.description: Lines 4 and 6 (+8) and restrictions; system readback.

steps.name: Correlation
steps.description: BOC: done with the readback. BOT: talk-on to correlate the target visually/by sensor.

steps.name: Attack
steps.description: "IP inbound, heading 270. Laser on" - "LASING 1688. CONTINUE" - "Laser SPOT" - "IN, 30 seconds, heading 230" - "CLEARED HOT" - "CLEARED HOT. Paveway one time, 30 seconds to impact, proceeding B25." (BMS JTAC: option 3 IP Inbound; request laser option 5, smoke option 6 - smoke lasts 1:00; target bullseye option 4.)

steps.name: Assess effectiveness
steps.description: Re-attack if no effect ("Same game plan, 9-line and restrictions. New TOT 15:37"); repeat steps 4-9 if the target moved or threats changed. (BMS JTAC asks for re-attack if targets remain; silence after an attack = wrong target or no effect.)

steps.name: Battle Damage Assessment
steps.description: "Good impacts, standby BDA" - "Target neutralized, Ground commander's intent met." (BMS JTAC: option 7 Check-Out gives the BDA.)

steps.name: Routing / Safety of Flight
steps.description: Check-out and routing away: "Fly B40 Block 26-28. Keep minimum 40 miles distance to echo point. Avoid all blocks below 26. Report established."

casProcedure.keyholeTemplate: Center E = echo point / wheel / overhead (target, target area or landmark). Sectors A/B/C/D with B = east; "B25 Block 20-22" = 25 NM east of E between 20,000 and 22,000 ft MSL (standard QNH).
bmsJtacPrerequisites: UHF preset 6 set (frequency from DTC); no AWACS/JSTARS needed.
Friendly unit (HQ, Infantry, Mechanized, Airmobile, Marine) within 10 NM of a target waypoint or within 6 NM of enemy forces.
Flight tasked in the ATO as CAS, On-Call CAS or Pre-Plan CAS.
CAS flight within 30 NM of the JTAC unit.

bmsJtacMenu.name: Check-In
bmsJtacMenu.description: Initial contact; press again to start the check-in.

bmsJtacMenu.name: Ready for Echo Point / 9-line
bmsJtacMenu.description: Receive echo point coordinates (N/E) and type of control; press again for the 9-line.

bmsJtacMenu.name: IP Inbound / Re-attack
bmsJtacMenu.description: Call IP inbound (readback lines 4+6(+8)); JTAC answers Cleared Hot. Recommended within about 3 NM of the IP. Also used for re-attack / next target.

bmsJtacMenu.name: Request Laser Marking (Lasing)
bmsJtacMenu.description: JTAC lases with the laser code set in the DTC/weapons UI and calls "Laser On" - use TGP LST mode.

bmsJtacMenu.name: Request Smoke Marking (Smoke)
bmsJtacMenu.description: Target marked with smoke for 1 minute; can be requested again.

bmsJtacMenu.name: Check-Out
bmsJtacMenu.description: JTAC provides BDA of your attacks.

bmsJtacMenu.name: Say Again
bmsJtacMenu.description: JTAC repeats last transmission on UHF.

casProcedure.menuAccess: Other agencies menu "y" (or "z") key, second page.
casProcedure.source: BMS Training Manual 4.38.1, Mission 27 (JTAC / CAS); BMS Comms & Nav Book 4.38.1 2.2.3

atcProcedures.title: Airbase comm plan and presets
steps: Agencies: Base Ops (placeholder), Ground, Tower, Approach/Departure (shared frequency), plus Common, Carrier (LSO) and Contingencies pages in the ATC menu ("t" key, repeated presses cycle pages: 1 Ground, 2 Tower, 3/4 Approach/Departure, 5 Common, 6 Carrier, 7 Contingencies).
ATC uses UHF only (VHF only for ATIS). Talking on the wrong frequency gets you redirected to the correct one.

UHF presets: 1 Ops, 2 Ground, 3 Tower, 4 Departure/Approach (departure base); 5 Tactical check-in (placeholder); 6 Tactical (AWACS) + JTAC; 7/8/9 arrival Approach/Tower/Ground; 10/11/12 alternate Approach/Tower/Ground; 13 Air refueling; 14 UHF common/Advisory 339.750 (F1 IVC); 20 LSO (carrier arrival).

VHF presets: 2 departure ATIS, 3 departure tower, 4 arrival tower, 7 arrival ATIS, 10 alternate ATIS, 11 alternate tower, 14 common 123.5, 15-19 intra-flight frequency of the 1st-5th flight in the package.
Typical sequence: UHF 2, 3, 4 outbound; 5/6 (and 13 for AAR) in flight; 4, 3, 2 on return.
A flight is a single entity for ATC: only the flight lead talks to ATC; wingmen just listen and switch when told.

atcProcedures.title: Getting ATIS
steps: Tune VHF to the ATIS frequency (charts / briefing).

ATIS gives airport name, information letter, active runway, wind, visibility and clouds (optionally as color code), temperature and altimeter setting. It loops continuously; changing the VHF frequency interrupts it.
BMS ATIS cannot differentiate left/right runways. Color code (set g_bUseATISColorCode 1): blue/white/green/yellow/amber/red; BLACK = airport closed.

atcProcedures.title: Ground - taxi for departure
steps: After ramp start, Ground gives the expected taxi time on UHF 2 (informative - not a clearance).
Be ready no later than 6 minutes before fragged take-off time.
Flight lead: "Request taxi for departure" (t3).

Possible answers: "Hold position" (stay, ATC will call back); "Give way to <callsign>"; "Taxi Papa, Alpha and hold short runway xx" (routing clearance; a hold short of a crossing runway followed by resumed routing = clearance to cross).

Taxi staggered; flight lead stops as close as possible to the runway hold lines (EOR closest spot) - ATC detects the lead position and calls "Contact tower, switch xxx.xx". If you do not hear it, move closer.

atcProcedures.title: Tower - take-off
steps: On tower frequency flight lead calls "Ready for departure" (tt1).

Answers: "Hold short" (traffic, or take-off time more than 3 min ahead - repeat "ready for departure" to request an earlier release); "Position and hold" (= line up and wait, not a take-off clearance); "Cleared for takeoff, runway xx" (normally preceded by wind); "Expedite departure" (clear the runway ASAP, rolling take-off if needed).
AI in the flight take off at 10 s intervals (rolling if expedite).
Stay on tower until the whole flight is airborne.

atcProcedures.title: Departure
steps: Once the whole flight is airborne call "Report airborne" (tttt1).
ATC answers "fly heading xxx" and/or "resume own navigation", terminating ATC service - switch to the mission frequency (usually tactical UHF 6).
Delaying the call until established on the SID usually gets you "resume own navigation" directly (the vector ignores SIDs).

atcProcedures.title: Approach - initial contact and recovery options
steps: Contact approach within about 20-30 NM (after checking destination ATIS); wingmen within 20 NM of lead are included in the flight, others must call separately.
Initial call states the number of aircraft: "Gunsan Approach, Falcon 1, 4 Ship F-16, 15 NM North West, 10 000 ft, request visual approach."

Options (approach page): 1 vectors for visual approach, 2 vectors for instrument approach, 3 overhead approach, unrestricted approach, 6 abort approach, 7 traffic in sight; "Heavy" call gets the longest runway if possible (4.37.2).
Descending through the transition level, set the QNH given by approach.

atcProcedures.title: Overhead recovery (break)
steps: Conditions: VMC, all flight members within 20 NM of lead at initial contact, traffic permitting. Not available on carriers.
Request overhead approach (ttt3); approach clears the flight in without vectors.

Fly to initial (AI: 10 NM from threshold; humans may use ~5 NM) in echelon close formation on the side opposite the break (echelon right for a left break). Break side is normally opposite the tower, decided by the lead.
At initial / within 10 NM approach switches the flight to tower; once all are on tower, lead calls request landing (tt2) before the break - tower clears inbound and asks to report the break.
Run in at 1000 ft AGL (AI) or 1500 ft AGL, around 300 kts. Lead reports the overhead break (tt5) - mandatory, with or without AI.
When lead turns final, tower detects him and clears the whole flight to land; no "report final" needed. Wingmen make no calls.

atcProcedures.title: Unrestricted approach (humans only)
steps: Request unrestricted approach on approach: fly any approach (instrument chart, overhead, straight-in, test profile) while keeping a place in the landing queue.
Switch to tower triggers automatically within 10 NM on the landing runway side; contact tower before final - it gives instructions or clears you to land. Reporting final is optional.
Deconfliction happens only on final - keep SA on other traffic.

atcProcedures.title: Formation landing
steps: Request unrestricted approach first.
On tower, request formation landing (tt3) instead of request landing (tt2).
Human pilots only, same flight, max 2-ship (split a 4-ship into 2-ships separated by at least 20 NM before contacting approach).

atcProcedures.title: Vectored visual approach
steps: Request vectors for visual approach (ttt1). Main AI recovery in VMC; denied if orbit altitude is in cloud, cloud layer under 8000 ft AGL when requested on top, visibility below VFR minima or airbase closed.

Each flight member is vectored separately. Geometry per runway: 4 holding points (stacked 1000 ft apart, depart at 4000 ft AGL, right-hand turns), 3 entry points and 2 base points (3000 ft AGL), 1 final approach point (8 NM, 2000 ft AGL).
Altitudes given by ATC are referenced to field elevation (QFE).
At the final approach point approach sends you to tower; report on final (tt4) no earlier than 6 NM (must be within +/-45 deg of the threshold or you are removed from the queue).

atcProcedures.title: Vectored instrument approach (ILS / radar)
steps: Use in IMC with the approach/radar charts. Denied if airport closed, crosswind above 25 kts, or weather below chart minima (without airbase.dat: clouds below 500 ft and visibility below 900 m).
Request vectors for instrument approach (ttt2) before overflying the IAF; flight members are vectored separately (1000 ft separation).
ATC uses 4 reference points (normally IAF ... final approach point) and gives heading/altitude/speed; overfly each point to get the next vector. Radar vector charts match these points best.
If vectors point back to a previous point, continue the procedure; if it goes wrong abort (ttt6) and request an unrestricted approach.
Example: "Vector for Instrument Approach" -> ATC confirms radar approach RWY 31 and QNH, "turn heading 100, descend and maintain 6000".
At the final approach point switch to tower and report final; tower clears you to land if detected in the final approach cone. At minima without runway in sight: go around.

atcProcedures.title: Missed approach / go-around
steps: Select "abort" on the tower page; tower acknowledges and tells you to recontact approach when able.
Fly the missed approach procedure on the chart (e.g. back to the IAF), then request a new approach or proceed to the alternate (alternate presets UHF 10/11/12).
An aborted approach on approach frequency is ttt6.

atcProcedures.title: After landing - EOR and taxi back
steps: After vacating the runway tower instructs to switch to ground; wait until the whole flight has vacated.
Humans-only flights proceed to the EOR if available (EOR procedure charts).
Request taxi back to the ramp (t4); ground assigns a taxi route and parking spot (check the airport parking chart).

atcProcedures.title: Contingencies - ground abort, say again, traffic
steps: Engine/jet stuck on the ground: use the Contingencies page (7th page) "Request Ground Abort n" for your flight position, otherwise the ATC queue behind you is blocked. AI behind the aborting human also abort; initial contact must be redone.
"Say Again" (ground, tower, approach pages): ATC repeats its last transmission - also tells a wingman whether he is in the landing queue.
Traffic calls under approach control: acknowledge with "Traffic in Sight" (ttt7).
A wingman wanting separate handling must first abort the approach (ttt6), then request his own approach.
Emergency tip: preset the backup UHF radio to the landing tower frequency to declare an emergency if systems fail.

tankerProcedures.title: Finding the tanker
steps: Tanker frequency is tied to the tanker callsign (e.g. Camel 1 = UHF 301.850, Canteen 1 = UHF 292.875). If your flight has a refuel point, the tanker is in the comm ladder and usually UHF preset 13.

Otherwise look up the tanker flight in the ATO / hover its map icon, or ask AWACS on tactical UHF 6: tactical menu page 2, option 4 "Vector to Tanker" (ATO-assigned tanker) or "Vector to Nearest Tanker" - AWACS gives position, TACAN channel and UHF frequency. No AWACS = no AAR; divert.
Set TACAN to the given channel in A-A TR (band toggled with 0 ENTR, mode with DCS right). KC-135 and KC-130H A-A TACAN give distance only; KC-10 gives distance and bearing.
Search with the FCR around FL200-240 (usual refuel altitude 20,000-24,000 ft, 280-300 kts).
tankerProcedures.source: BMS Comms & Nav Book 4.38.1 2.2.2; BMS Training Manual 4D.1

tankerProcedures.title: Pre-tanker checks and request
steps: Before entering the 10 NM tanker bubble: emitters (radar, TACAN, IFF, ECM, radar altimeter) safe or off; Master Arm safe; external lights per briefing/SOP. Radar to standby once visual (nose cold).

Within 10 DME: tanker menu ("y") option 1 "Request Air Flight Refueling" (whole flight), or "Request Air Individual Refueling" / "Request Air Element Refueling". Outside 10 NM the tanker gives heading and distance for rejoin.

Tanker clears you to pre-contact and lowers the boom. Open the AIR REFUEL door (FUEL panel) - blue RDY light on the right indexer; limits: open below 400 KCAS / M0.85, fly open below 420 KCAS / M0.95. Do not open too early (about 5 NM or at the observation position) to avoid trapped fuel in depressurized tanks.
Select DED BNGO page (LIST 2) to monitor fuel transfer.
tankerProcedures.source: BMS Comms & Nav Book 4.38.1 2.2.2; BMS Training Manual 4D.1; TO 1F-16CM/AM-1 BMS 37.6

tankerProcedures.title: Rejoin
steps: Tanker flies about 300-305 kts. Closure rate limit 10 kts per 1000 ft: over 2 NM 100 kts, 6000 ft 60 kts, 3000 ft 30 kts, inside 1000 ft max 10 kts overtake. Offset to the left side to judge closure.
Rear aspect (point parallel) intercept: pursue behind the tanker 2-10 line.

Head-on (fighter turn-on) intercept: offset ~8-9 NM from the track; at the tanker 2 or 10 o'clock, 15 NM, start a 30 deg bank turn at 350-420 kts; halfway the tanker is at 12-1 o'clock ~5 NM; roll out ~2.5 NM in trail and close.
Flight lead / single ship goes to pre-contact; others to the observation position (echelon left on the tanker's left wing).

tankerProcedures.title: Pre-contact, contact and fuel transfer
steps: Stabilize in pre-contact: about 50 ft below at 30 deg down from the tanker; align the gun cross with the lower boom and the HUD side mounts with the inboard engines. No director lights yet.

Boom operator: "<callsign>, cleared to contact position"; red F (forward) and U (up) director lights come on. Move forward slowly (small throttle bursts) following the lights (steady = correction, blinking = fine tuning) until they go off.

Boom connects: RDY off, green AR/NWS light on. Call "Goblin 31, Contact". Hold the sight picture using the director lights (left row U/D elevation, right row F/A telescoping; red far, yellow close, green ideal) - fix one axis at a time, relax.
Tanker gives a heads-up before turning (30 deg bank for 180 deg turns) - stay in position, match attitude, add a little power.
Call "1000 lbs to go" on UHF to alert the next receiver.
Transfer rate: about 2000 lb/min (KC-135, two pumps), 3000 lb/min (KC-10/KDC-10).

tankerProcedures.title: Disconnect and reform
steps: Press A/R DISC on the stick at the desired fuel: amber DISC light momentarily, AR/NWS off, blue RDY back on.
Retard slightly and slide to the tanker's right wing (reform area, echelon right).
Tanker menu option 3 "Done Refueling" - removes you from the queue so the next receiver is cleared to pre-contact.
When the whole flight is done, the aircraft that requested the refueling must select option 4 "Terminate Flight Refuel" (since 4.37.4).
In the reform area close the AR door (no indexer lights), CNI page back, FCR out of OVRD, check fuel balance.
Departing receivers move at least 1 NM left or right of track before climbing ahead of the tanker.
tankerProcedures.source: BMS Comms & Nav Book 4.38.1 2.2.2; BMS Training Manual 4D.3; TO 1F-16CM/AM-1 BMS 37.9

tankerProcedures.title: Quick flow
steps: Default for BMS AI: while lead refuels, the next receiver waits in the on-deck position (close echelon left, route formation ~10 ft) and moves to pre-contact as soon as the boom is free; finished receivers go to the tanker's right wing.
Human flights: use only when conditions and skills permit (VMC only); coordinate with the tanker ("Quick Flow" in the initial call).
Breakaway during quick flow: the on-deck receiver follows the receiver on the boom; receivers on the wing stay with the tanker.

tankerProcedures.title: Breakaway (emergency separation)
steps: Call on the AAR frequency: tanker callsign + "breakaway" three times, e.g. "Chevy 2, breakaway, breakaway, breakaway" (abnormal closure, overrun, engine failure...).
Disconnect, retard throttle and establish a definite descent (speed brake if needed), drop aft until the whole tanker is in sight.
If visual is lost, descend at least 500 ft below the tanker.
Tanker accelerates in level flight. If called before receivers reach observation, the whole receiver flight breaks away; otherwise only the contact/pre-contact receiver.

tankerProcedures.title: Probe and drogue (basket) refueling
steps: Since 4.36 probe-equipped receivers (F/A-18, Mirage 2000, Harrier, MiG-29 and more) can refuel from compatible tankers (KC-135, KC/DC-10, KC-130H, C-160R NG, IL-78M).
F-15C: same boom procedure as the F-16 but the receptacle is on the left behind the canopy - offset slightly right of the boom.

awacsCalls.meaning: AWACS reports the overall picture (up to 3 groups fully): "Cobra 2-1, Magic 1, Picture is multiple groups range and azimuth split". Single group: "Falcon 1, Sentry 1, picture is one group, bullseye XXX/YY NM, hot, hostile."

Range split: all contacts within 10 deg of azimuth (groups labelled Lead, Centre, Trail). Azimuth split: within 10 NM of range with more than 10 deg azimuth difference (cardinal labels, e.g. West/East group; Centre if exactly between). Range & azimuth split: neither. More than 3 groups: "picture is multiple groups".
LABEL group, bullseye/BRAA XXX/XX, XX thousand, ASPECT, ID. Above 25 NM bullseye (if radio calls use bullseye option), under 25 NM BRAA.
HOT 180-120 deg, BEAMING 120-80 deg, DRAGGING 80-40 deg, COLD 40-0 deg. At long range AWACS uses TRACK [cardinal direction] instead.

awacsCalls.call: ID: Friendly / Bogey / Bandit / Hostile / Furball
awacsCalls.meaning: Identification based on the declare criteria; Furball when friendlies are mixed with hostiles.

Bug a target on the FCR and ask its ID: "Sentry 1, Falcon 1, Declare" -> "Falcon 1, Sentry 1, Furball, 2 friendly, 3 bandit" when friendlies and hostiles are within 4 NM / 10,000 ft of the locked contact.

awacsCalls.call: Vector to Nearest Air Threat (Bogey Dope)
awacsCalls.meaning: Tactical menu page 2 option 1: "Cobra 2, Magic 1, nearest threat BRAA 345/19 miles 25 thousand, beaming, Hostile, Print Mig-21, 2 ship." (bullseye outside 25 NM, BRAA inside).

awacsCalls.call: Vector to Tanker / Vector to Nearest Tanker
awacsCalls.meaning: Tactical menu page 2 option 4 (ATO tanker) or nearest tanker: AWACS gives tanker position, TACAN channel and UHF frequency.
Since 4.38 AWACS/GCI threat alerts (hot fighters only) are repeated every 10 NM until you acknowledge with JUDY: the crew has radar/visual contact and runs the intercept, controller minimizes calls.
Second page of the tactical menu gives radar vectors for specific situations: nearest threat, tanker, alternate airbase, carrier group, etc.

Tactical net menu with the "q" (or "a") key; must be on the package tactical frequency (UHF preset 6) and an AWACS must be airborne on station. Another AWACS may take over on the same frequency with another callsign.
GCI: vector 060, Angels 23 (23,000 ft), contact is a Bandit, possible Renegade; go Buster (MIL), not Gate (afterburner).

radioCallFormat.title: Basic call structure
radioCallFormat.description: Station called first, then own callsign, then the message. Replies reverse the order ("Cyborg 7, Eyeball 9, send your check-in").

radioCallFormat.title: Initial contact with approach
radioCallFormat.example: Gunsan Approach, Falcon 1, 4 Ship F-16, 15 NM North West, 10 000 ft, request visual approach.
radioCallFormat.description: Agency, callsign, number and type of aircraft (defines what ATC treats as the flight), position, altitude, request.

radioCallFormat.title: AWACS picture
radioCallFormat.example: Falcon 1 Sentry 1, picture is three groups, range split. Lead group bullseye XXX/YY NM, hot, hostile. Centre group bullseye AAA/BB NM, beaming, bandit. Trail group bullseye CCC/DD NM, beaming, bogey.
radioCallFormat.description: Picture label, then one line per group: label, bullseye/BRAA, altitude, aspect, ID.

radioCallFormat.title: BRAA / bogey dope
radioCallFormat.example: Cobra 2, Magic 1, nearest threat BRAA 345/19 miles 25 thousand, beaming, Hostile, Print Mig-21, 2 ship.
radioCallFormat.description: Bearing / range, altitude, aspect, ID, type and number.

radioCallFormat.title: Declare / Furball
radioCallFormat.example: Sentry 1, Falcon 1, Declare. -> Falcon 1, Sentry 1, Furball, 2 friendly, 3 bandit.
radioCallFormat.description: Ask ID of the contact under your FCR lock.

radioCallFormat.title: HARM launch (PET)
radioCallFormat.example: Weasel 3-1, Magnum PET Alpha 2 minutes. ... Weasel 3-1, PET Alpha timeout.
radioCallFormat.description: UHF call on HARM launch so aircraft in the vicinity know when to enter the SAM WEZ; timeout call when the TUI counter reaches zero.

radioCallFormat.title: CAS check-in
radioCallFormat.example: Eyeball 9, Cyborg 7, Mission number 2024, two by F-16C, Currently Bravo 25, block 20-22, 510 rounds of 20 mike mike, four by GBU-54 each aircraft, Nose/Tail fusing, Laser code 1688 each aircraft, Playtime four zero minutes, FAC(A) capable, Sniper, IDM 11 and 12 sweet, Abort Code: Oscar November.
radioCallFormat.description: Mission number, aircraft, position/altitude, ordnance, laser codes, playtime, capabilities, abort code.

radioCallFormat.title: Authentication
radioCallFormat.example: Cyborg 7, Eyeball 9, Code word "Bravo 1" in effect, Authenticate Tango Alpha. -> Eyeball 9, Cyborg 7, Authenticate Romeo.
radioCallFormat.description: Challenge with two letters, answer with the letter between them in the codeword.

radioCallFormat.title: CAS attack sequence
radioCallFormat.example: Eyeball 9, Cyborg 71. IP inbound, heading 270. Laser on. -> LASING 1688. CONTINUE. -> Laser SPOT. -> IN, 30 seconds, heading 230. -> Cyborg 71, CLEARED HOT. -> CLEARED HOT. Paveway one time, 30 seconds to impact, proceeding B25.
radioCallFormat.description: No release without clearly hearing CLEARED HOT.

radioCallFormat.title: Abort (CAS)
radioCallFormat.example: Cyborg 7, Eyeball 9, ABORT UNIFORM, ABORT UNIFORM, ABORT UNIFORM. -> Cyborg 7 aborts the pass.
radioCallFormat.description: With abort code; in the clear "ABORT, ABORT, ABORT" if none was passed.

radioCallFormat.title: Time hack
radioCallFormat.example: Cyborg 71, Eyeball 9, TIME TO TARGET 5 minutes. READY, READY, HACK.
radioCallFormat.description: Start the ICP time page hack (ICP 6, NEXT) on HACK.

radioCallFormat.title: Talk-on
radioCallFormat.example: Cyborg 71, SLEW to line 4 and 6. Describe what you see. -> I see five circular training targets. ... -> Cyborg 71, CONTACT. ... -> Roger, the most eastern truck is your target. -> Cyborg 71, CAPTURED.
radioCallFormat.description: Correlation from a common reference point to the target.

radioCallFormat.title: Check-out
radioCallFormat.example: Eyeball 9, Cyborg 7 is checking out. We are Dakota and have no playtime left. -> Cyborg 7, Eyeball 9 roger. Fly B40 Block 26-28. Keep minimum 40 miles distance to echo point. Avoid all blocks below 26. Report established.
radioCallFormat.description: Routing out of the CAS area.

radioCallFormat.title: AAR contact / breakaway
radioCallFormat.example: Goblin 31, Contact. ... Chevy 2, breakaway, breakaway, breakaway.
radioCallFormat.description: Contact call when connected; breakaway = tanker callsign + breakaway x3.

radioCallFormat.title: Radio discipline in BMS
radioCallFormat.description: ATC does not require readbacks and often issues the next instruction immediately (reading back can step on comms). Only flight leads talk to ATC. BMS ATC uses both "hold position" (stay where you are) and "position and hold" (line up and wait).

iffModes.description: Military, non-cryptographic, codes 00-73 (first digit max 7, second max 3; e.g. 41, 22 valid, 44, 81 invalid). Normally mission type/role. Change: enter 2-digit code + ENTR on the IFF page; toggle active with ICP 1 + ENTR. EMER reply: 70.
Military, non-cryptographic, codes 0000-7777 (digits max 7). Unique aircraft identification code. Change: enter "2" + 4-digit code + ENTR; toggle with ICP 2 + ENTR. EMER reply: 7777.
Military and civil (ATC), codes 0000-7777. Change: enter a 3- or 4-digit code + ENTR; toggle with ICP 3 + ENTR. EMER reply: 7700.
Civil: pressure altitude reply (no code). Toggle with ICP 5 + ENTR. Normal reply in EMER.

Military cryptographic mode (closest to true IFF): rapid encrypted challenges that must be answered with the same key. Key cannot be changed directly - toggle keys A/B with ICP 6 + ENTR; toggle active with ICP 4 + ENTR. Feedback option (ICP 7 + ENTR): OUT (none, default), LIT (4 highlighted on CNI when interrogated), AUD (plus tone when the interrogation key does not match) - AUD recommended. IFF caution light when Mode 4 is interrogated but cannot reply (zeroized/uncoded/disabled). M-4 CODE switch A/B, HOLD, ZERO.
Updated version of Mode 4 - not implemented in BMS.
Updated civil mode - visual representation only (ICP 8 + ENTR toggle not implemented; M3/MS backup position Mode S not implemented).

OFF (unpowered), STBY (powered, no replies), LOW (normal, replies at half range), NORM (interrogate and reply), EMER (interrogate; replies with emergency codes Mode 1 70, Mode 2 7777, Mode 3 7700, Mode C and 4 normal). IFF IDENT button is non-functional.

LIST RCL (INTG) pages; SCAN interrogation with TMS left < 0.6 s (coupled to FCR scan volume in CPL, full +/-60 deg 8-beam scan in DCPL), up to 32 replies; LOS mode interrogates along the line of sight. SCAN and LOS keep independent modes/codes. ATC and AWACS do not interrogate in BMS; AI fighters may interrogate in BVR. IFF only confirms friendlies - no/invalid reply = bogey, not hostile.

IFF policy is loaded from the DTC: up to 12 TIME events (Zulu time) and POS events (cardinal direction from a steerpoint) change modes/codes automatically; STAT page P/T field shows enabled/occurred events.

aiCommands.note: Wingman menu talks to #2 (or #4 from #3); element menu to #3/#4; flight menu to all. In an air-to-air engagement direct elements (element menu) - the flight cannot be directed as a whole. AI stay on their assigned VHF intra-flight frequency and follow your UHF changes.

Attack My Target, Buddy Spike, Raygun, Weapons Free AA, Weapons Free AG, Weapons Hold (default; AI ask permission, no answer in 30 s = cleared), Check Your Six, Clear My Six, Attack Targets (sort doctrine).
Rejoin, Split Wing, Glue Wing, Drop Stores, Drop Fuel Tanks, Datalink Ground Tgt, Go Shooter, Go Cover.

Offensive Pursuit, Offensive Split, Beam Deploy, Grinder (6 NM trail), Wide Azimuth (issue before 30 NM), Short Azimuth (within 15 NM), Sweep (before 35 NM), Defensive (pump away, threats outside 30 NM).
Current Altitude Attack, High Attack (15000 ft MSL), Low Attack (3500 ft above target, 1500 ft for high drag), Dive Attack (20 deg), Popup Attack (offset starts 5 NM, stops 3.5 NM), Free Attack.
Resume Mission, Return to Base, Snooze Radar, Activate Radar, Say Position, Say Damage Report, Say Status, Say Fuel State (hundreds of lbs: 83 = 8300 lbs), Say Weapon State, Take the Lead.

Close Up / Kickout (x2 distance), Switch Side, Break Right/Left, Stack High/Level/Low, Go Deck (400 ft AGL), Flex; Wedge, Trail, Ladder, Stack, Fluid, Spread, Arrowhead, Higher/Lower (1000 ft); flight only: Box, Res Cell, Vic, Line Abreast, Finger Four, Echelon Left/Right, Diamond.

Fence In (lights off/covert, Master Arm on), Fence Out (lights on, Master Arm off), Lights S.O.P., Music On/Off (ECM), Smoke On/Off, Switch Flight Uniform/Victor (for backup UHF use), Set Bingo (AI copy your DED bingo).
Single Ship, Element (default echelon, lead on downwind side), Echelon (4-ship, flight menu), Four Ship Three In, Four Ship Four In.

glossary.meaning: To track air emitters such as refuellers, the tacan needs to be set to Air-Air track and receive.
Air Defence Identification Zone. A forward limit of national airspace.
Above Ground Level: Altitude given above the ground.
The preplanned point on or near target that is used to align pipper
American Standard Code for Information Interchange
Attack Target Complex (a type of Mission Assignment) , Air Traffic Controller
Attitude Bars and Horizon Line/Flight Path Marker
Weapon deliver options stored in SMS that are anticipated to be used in specific instances
Automatic Brightness control to maintain, contrast ration between the symbols and background
Airborne Early Warning and Control System
The Fresnel lens situated left of the landing deck guiding pilot on the optimal glidepath.
A threshold fuel value that the pilot enters in MMC memory
Air-to-Ground weapon delivery modes that utilize radar ground map features rather than indicators to locate the target
A deck landing where the hook misses all 4 wires
Base Recovery Course. o Carriers: The heading of the landing deck during aircraft operations (Minus 10 from the carrier's heading). o LHD: The course of the LHD
Brevity for directing aircraft to begin their approach procedure.
Day position allows control of brightness from off to full intensity
The removal of display data from the HUD/ MFD/HMCS (Declutter)
The 4 way switch on the ICP.
Data Entry Display, Dedicated Channel Mode

Decision Height. The height (height is always referring to vertical distance above ground) at which the pilot needs to transition from instrument flight to visual flight. At that point, the pilot needs to have visually acquired the runway to be allowed to continue the approach.
Distance measuring equipment. Gives the distance between your aircraft and the selected radio- navigation station.

Desired Out Range: range from the closest group where an out maneuver defeats any weapons in the air or on the jet and preserves distance to recommit with launch-and-decide tactics. DOR = DR + adversary closing range while aborting and recommitting.

Decision Range: minimum range at which an aircraft can execute the briefed notch, hold it for a pre-briefed time to defeat spikes, then abort/exit and remain outside the threat max stern WEZ. DR = STERN WEZ + adversary closing range during 15 s notch + margin.
Flight path marker with drift cutout
The zone in which a missile would strike a maneuvering target
Elevation - The height of the terrain above sea level (airports, structure).
Forward Edge of the Battle Area
Flight Information Region - airspace category around an ATC center.
A device used to initiate weapon detonation
The maximum number of g's allowed by the flight controls
The maximum number of g's that can be pulled without losing current specific gravity
Guided Bomb Unit, conventional bomb with selfcontained guidance system
Ground Moving Target, Greenwich Mean Time
Global Position System: A system allowing precise navigation using 3 navigation satellites.
Ground Stabilized, Glide slope, Geographic Specificity
Glideslope: The horizontal beam of the ILS allowing the pilot to fly the correct slope (usually 3°) to the runway threshold.
Horn Awareness and Recovery Training Series
Jettison mode ready indication (Weapons selected released unarmed)
Horizontal Situation Instrument. The main navigation instrument to track radials.
Intraflight Data Link, Initialization Data Load

Instrument Landing System. A radio beam to help pilots land on a specific runway in poor visibility. The beam is made of a horizontal radio wave to guide pilots onto the glideslope and a vertical wave to guide pilots onto the runway centerline (localizer).
Instrument Meteorological Conditions - the IFR regime.
Intensity, Transfer of Initialization Data , Internal
Wind correction constant due to altitude gain
Low Altitude Navigation Targeting Infrared For Night
Localizer: the vertical beam of the ILS allowing the pilot the align his aircraft with the runway centerline.
Laser Spot Tracker, Land Specific Type
Mode, Multiple, Mask, Master, Mass Model, Meters, Mission Store
MASTER ARM switch, Matrix Assembly, Medium

Minimum Abort Range: range at which a standard abort maneuver kinematically defeats any missiles and momentarily keeps the aircraft outside the adversary WEZ. MAR = max F-POLE of adversary shot + your turn radius + margin.
The area where aircraft hold in preparation for approach
Minimum Detectable Signal, Mission Data Set
Mass Data Transfer, Mission Data Table
Mark, a designation preceding model numbers
Military Operation Area: a limited zone where military training exercise occurs (live firing, dogfights, artillery ...).
Brevity for the carrier (or surname for the mother ship)

Marker beacon. Along the ILS track, we often find 3 markers (outer, middle and inner) that are limited radio emissions emitting vertically at set distances from the runway threshold. They are seen in the cockpit through the MRK BCN green light, next to the HSI that blinks at a specific frequency according to the overflown marker. (In civil aircraft, each marker has its own colored light but in the F-16, the light is always green). An audible code is also emitted when overflying the marker.
Minimum Recommit Range: minimum range at which the fighter can recommit, target and employ MRM while turning and remain outside the STERN WEZ (threat hot).
Mean Sea Level: Generally referring to altitude above sea level.
Minimum Shot Range: minimum range at which the MRM must be launched to achieve an active state and be out no later than MAR.
Minimum Targeting Range: range at which flight members share targeting within a group to ensure group elimination; decision tool to target wingmen (outside MTR) or flight leads (inside MTR).
Notice to Airman. Notices are published periodically. Hazards to navigation and others are mentioned in the NOTAM. Each pilot needs to give NOTAM proper consideration.
LSO callsign. (Basically, the tower for carrier landings. Comes from the time of antiquities when LSO's used paddles).

Precision Approach Path Indicator. A row of 4 lights placed on the side of the runway to visually indicate the optimal glide slope. Lights can be either white or red depending on the position of the aircraft landing. Red means too low, white means too high. The correct glide slope is indicated when 2 lights are white and 2 lights are red.
Program, Precision Guided Munition The act of depressing weapon release button Optical sight aim dot
The point in a Case III approach, at 5000 feet MSL, all aircraft will decrease their rate-of-descent to less than 2000 feet per minute and continue let-down to a 10 NM DME fix.

Transition Altitude: The altitude where the local altimeter setting is changed to the universal altimeter setting (29.92 inch of mercury or 1013 hPa). From ground to Transition Altitude, measurements are in Feet.

Transition level. Above the Trans Level, we refer to altitudes in Flight Levels (20000ft = FL200). Descending from FL150 to 3500ft with a trans level of FL70, we will switch the universal altimeter setting from 29.92 (1013 hPa) to the local altimeter setting at FL70 (7000ft).

Visual Approach Slope Indicator: A Visual aid to gauge glideslope when landing visually. In Falcon, it's made of two rows of lights each side of the runway. The lights turn white to red depending on the aircraft position on the glideslope. Mnemonic: Red over white is alright - red is dead.
